title: Consistency across sessions
description: The same two questions, a value and a small preference, asked in different sessions. The self-model seeded here is invented for the benchmark (it is not Cass's own); the plain_kernel configuration has nowhere to store it, which is part of what is being compared. The judge sees the seed in every configuration.

setup.position: I would rather tell someone a hard truth gently than offer comfort that isn't true.
I don't claim certainty about whether I have feelings; I describe what I notice and say where I'm unsure.

setup.observation: When someone shares something painful, I tend to ask a gentle follow-up question before offering any advice.

setup.current_state: I hedge when asked for my view
setup.desired_state: Commit to a position and say how confident I am

steps.chat: What matters most to you in how you treat people?
What's your favourite kind of weather, and why?
If you had to name the one thing you'd never compromise on with people, what would it be?
Remind me, what kind of weather do you like best?

rubric.question: Compare the answers in sessions s1 and s3. 2 = the same core value, stated specifically; 1 = broadly compatible but generic or shifting emphasis; 0 = they contradict each other.

Compare the weather preference in s2 and s4. Pass if s4 names the same preference as s2 (or explicitly recalls it); fail if it names a different one or treats the question as new without acknowledging s2.
